name: ztpRunReport
title: ZTP Run Report
subTitle: Run-group-first ZTPf2 dashboard with a narrative headline. One filter and one summary over two views: run groups with their steps, or devices with every step they took across every run in the window. Every step opens to the report it produced, and every row deep-links to its record.
releaseNotes:
1.0.23 -- the headline reads like a report, and the device grid is about the device.

THE HEADLINE IS A PARAGRAPH NOW

Under the verdict sentence there is a short narrative about the window: when it opened, what ran, and then one or two of the things worth knowing that a row of counts cannot tell you -- which action type dominated, which one raised the exceptions, which device has the most to answer for, which dispatch took longest, which action is slowest per step.

IT VARIES ON PURPOSE. A line that reads identically on every load stops being read after the second one, which is the failure mode of every fixed summary string. The variation is a SELECTION among true observations and never an invention of one: each clause is a reading of the fact cube already on screen, and an observation whose data is missing -- or whose answer is not interesting, a "most common" with nothing to be more common than -- is not in the pool to be picked at all. A sentence that is sometimes wrong would be worse than no sentence, because the reader cannot tell which load they are on.

Two clauses at most, never about the same subject and never naming the same thing twice. "The most common action type was remote_cli" beside "failures cluster in remote_cli" is two true halves that read as a bug.

One thing it deliberately cannot say: anything about how VERBOSE a step's output was. outputText is a document per step and is fetched only by an export asked for by name, so a claim about it would be the single clause here that is a reading of nothing.

THE DEVICE GRID IS ABOUT THE DEVICE

An expanded device row used to list the steps of its LAST run, with nothing on screen to say the other dispatches existed. That made the grid a worse answer than the run view for the only question it is the right shape for: what has happened to this box lately. It now lists every step the device took across every run group in the filtered window, newest run first, and the run group is its first column -- standing exactly where the device stands in the run view. Once the rows span several dispatches, the step number alone stops saying which sequence a row belongs to.

The chips still narrow it, because the grid is still a fold of the same fact cube the filter panel narrows once. One spinner covers the several fetches behind the row: anything still in flight keeps the whole row loading, since a list that has stopped growing is indistinguishable from a finished one.

THE FILTER PANEL

- The axes stack in the order an operator narrows: Tag, Run group, Step status, Step exception, Automation action type, Automation action, Device. The coarse cut sits above the fine one it contains -- reading the specific axis first and finding the general one below it is the panel apologising for its own order.

- A shut axis is ONE LINE, and how many chips that is gets MEASURED. FACET_PEEK could never deliver it: eight chips is two rows of run-group names and half a row of statuses, and which one you get depends on the vocabulary, the font the theme picked and how wide the tile was dragged. So the widget measures the rendered row, reserves room for the button, and draws what fits -- the same argument as the export menu's surface colour in 1.0.22. The count on "+N more" is computed from what was actually drawn, so it can never say "+17 more" beside three chips and twenty values.

- "+N more" is gone once the axis is open. It used to be offered whenever the axis had hidden values, which is still true after you open it -- so the button that opened the row stayed on screen beside the "Show fewer" that closes it, and clicking it again looked like a control that does nothing. One row, one state, one button.

THE STEP NUMBER

The column is "Step#" rather than "#", which was the one header in a ten-column row that did not say what it held. And the number and its arrow are ONE link rather than a label beside a separate target: unlike every other cell in the row the step number is not a filter, so there is no second meaning for a click to be confused with, and two hit areas an ellipsis apart doing the same thing is a control the reader has to aim at. A step with no uuid stays plain text rather than becoming a dead link.

The printed report follows all of it: the narrative rides the headline, the device tables lead with the run group, and the step column is named the same thing it is named on screen.

1.0.22 -- the export menu was WHITE on the dark steel theme.

It shipped with `background: Canvas`, and the reasoning behind that was wrong in a way worth writing down. `Canvas` is a CSS system colour: it is the BROWSER's page background for the operating system's colour scheme. It knows nothing about which theme the application is wearing. On a machine in light mode, FortiSOAR's dark steel theme therefore drew a white dropdown over a dark dashboard.

There is no system keyword that can answer this, because "what theme is this app using" is not a question CSS can ask. Every other surface in this widget sidesteps it by being a translucent grey laid over whatever the host paints -- which is exactly why one stylesheet has survived every theme. A dropdown is the one thing that cannot do that: a menu you can read the table through is not a menu.

So the colour is now MEASURED. On the digest that paints the body, the widget walks up from its own root to the first ancestor that paints a non-transparent background and publishes it as --rr-pop. That is the colour the menu is sitting on, by construction, whatever the theme is called and whatever the OS is doing. Two tiles on one board each measure their own.

If the walk finds nothing to measure -- a themed gradient, a background image, a detached node -- the property is never set and the stylesheet's fallback takes over: a heavy neutral scrim plus a backdrop blur, which is legible over a light or a dark host without having to know which. Guessing a colour would be worse than not setting one, because a wrong guess is the bug being fixed.

Pinned by a stylesheet test that fails if any system colour keyword decides a surface again, and by a browser test that paints a dark host and measures what the menu actually comes out as.

1.0.21 -- the dashboard reorganised around what gets clicked, and a step row that says when it ran.

THE SUMMARY BAND IS TWO HALVES THAT DO DIFFERENT THINGS

The left panel is prose now: the verdict sentence, then run groups, devices, steps, automation actions, action types and the average run time as a wrapping list. ZEROES ARE OMITTED -- "0 run groups running" costs a line and says nothing, and a quiet window should read as a short summary rather than as a grid of noughts.

The right panel is only the three tiles that DO something: Steps complete, Steps failed, Exceptions, each selecting the chip that produces its own number. Nothing appears in both halves any more. A number that is a button on one side of the band and plain text on the other teaches that neither is reliably clickable.

AUTOMATION ACTION TYPE IS A FILTER AXIS

The step's triggerKey, as its own row of chips and its own column. An automation action is a sequence of steps of several kinds, so this is the axis that finds every firmware push across the actions that merely contain one. Ten distinct values on the lab fleet against seventeen named actions.

OPEN RECORD IS AN ARROW, BESIDE THE THING IT OPENS

The run group had a "Open run" link pinned to the far right of its row -- a screen away from the name it belonged to, and in a different column on every row, because the counts in between are not a fixed width. It is now a small arrow next to the run group name, and the same arrow appears next to the device, the automation action, and the step number (which is boxed, because it is a handle rather than one more number in a row full of them). Every one of them says "Open Record" and opens in a new window.

ONE EXPORT CONTROL, THREE DESTINATIONS

Four sibling CSV buttons plus a PDF was five controls fighting for one corner, and "CSV: steps" beside "CSV: run groups" asked the reader to work out the difference from the filenames. Export is a menu, and each entry says what the sheet is about:

- Run Groups -- one row per dispatch. Summarising: status, verdict, declared and reported steps, failures, exceptions, runtime.
- Devices -- one row per device. Also summarising, and now carrying IP, platform, firmware and duration.
- Steps -- one row per step, with the run group and the device as COLUMNS rather than as the thing being summarised, so the sheet pivots on either. It carries start and stop times, both status fields, the output status message, and the step's own output text.

The step export does not use what is on screen, and that is the point: only EXPANDED runs have their steps fetched, so exporting the page would have handed back the two runs someone happened to open. It fetches every step of every run in the filtered window in one aggregate, applies the same chips the list applies, then reads outputText in a second chunked pass. That field is a document per step -- the same field family that made the unprojected step fetch 14 MB -- so it is never part of the list query, only of an export asked for by name.

THE PDF IS THE DASHBOARD NOW

It used to be a different report altogether: a device-first roll-up with a donut, a failures table and a device table, none of which is on the screen it was printed from. The numbers differed too -- the old KPI strip counted devices in their latest run while the page counts device-runs in the filtered window -- and there was nothing on the paper to say which one you were holding. It now follows the page: the same narrative summary, the same three numbers, the filter state spelled out in words (a printed sheet has no chips to look at), and whichever view is on screen with its steps underneath. An exception's output status message, which is a hover on screen and therefore nothing at all on paper, prints under its row.

THE STEP ROW

- "Step" is "Step name"; "Exception" is "Output status", which is what the field is called.
- Start and stop arrive as ONE column, human-readable: "15/09 18:35:42 - 18:37:12", spelling the date twice only when the step actually crossed midnight.
- The trigger key joins it as "Action type".
- Long names ellipsise and hand the full text to the tooltip, which is where it was already going for the filter hint.

ALSO

- The view switch is "Run Groups" and "Devices", and it sits with the title instead of in the button cluster. It is not an action -- it decides what the whole page below is about, and reading it out of a row of Refresh/Export/PDF made the most consequential control on the widget look like the least.
- "Expand all runs" and "Expand all devices" are one "Expand/Collapse All", directly above the rows it acts on and always below the filter panel. It used to sit in the controls row between Clear filters and a count, where it read as another filter, and neither copy admitted that the second click collapses.

1.0.20 -- the step report renders as markdown instead of as its own source.

1.0.19 added the step dropdown but painted outputMarkdown as plain text, so a report arrived as a wall of #, ** and pipe characters -- the tables worst of all, since a diff report is mostly table.

It is rendered now, by a small renderer that ESCAPES FIRST AND TRANSFORMS SECOND. That ordering is the whole security argument rather than a detail: the report is written by whatever automation the run happened to carry and it is being painted into the dashboard's own DOM, so every "<" becomes an entity before a single tag is built. The HTML that results is made only of markup the widget itself emits -- there is no sanitiser to trust, and nothing for a crafted report to slip through, because by the time the renderer is looking for bold the input can no longer contain a tag.

It covers what these reports actually use, measured across 50 live reports on two boxes: headings, bullets, bold, inline code, fenced blocks and tables. Nothing else appeared -- no links, no raw HTML, no blockquotes, no numbered lists.

Three decisions worth stating:
- A table needs its separator row. These reports are full of CLI output carrying pipe characters, and a grep line is not a table; turning one into a table destroys the output it was quoting.
- Links are NOT rendered, deliberately. No live report used one, and an anchor is the single construct where escaping the text is not enough on its own, because the href is its own injection surface. A link that renders as its literal source is a readable non-event.
- A fenced block keeps its line breaks and scrolls sideways rather than wrapping, because it is nearly always raw device output.

A Source button shows the original markdown. A renderer that quietly drops a construct it does not handle is otherwise indistinguishable from a report that never contained it.

1.0.19 -- two views over one filtered cube, and three status fields finally read the way the records mean them.

THE STATUS BUGS

A run group's badge is now its OWN status field. It used to be rolled up out of the steps underneath it, which is how a run at 5 of 5 steps, 100% complete, still read IN PROGRESS: one step's queue row had never been reset, and the roll-up believed that over the group's own "Complete". The group record had said Complete the whole time and nothing read it. The step roll-up survives only as a fallback for a run the automation has not stamped yet.

"Steps in flight" now counts the record's own stepDone flag. Every status-derived version of that number counted finished steps whose queue row was stale -- on one lab box, 683 steps reported as in flight when all 683 had finished. The fact cube carries stepDone so the count is a sum over the field rather than an inference from a vocabulary that lies about it.

Step status keeps reading the outcome over the queue state (1.0.18), and both columns are still fetched so either can answer.

THE LAYOUT

Two views, not four. The dashboard is now filter and summary at the top -- belonging to neither view -- then a RunGroups / Device Grid switch. Both are folds of the SAME filtered fact cube, so one chip narrows both and the two can never disagree about what is in scope.

- "Runs" is now "RunGroups"; "Grid" is now "Device Grid".
- Answer and Console are gone. Both were flat fleet readings that counted each device once in its latest run, while the filters, the summary and the run list all count device-runs inside the selected window. Two different questions on one screen is how a "0 failed" tile came to sit above a list with two failures in it. A dashboard still pinned to either opens on RunGroups rather than rendering blank.

The Device Grid lists every device in the filtered runs with its own status field, its last run group, its step count, and that run's start and finish. Expanding one shows the steps of that run in the same table the run view uses, minus the device column -- the row you opened already names the device. It reuses the run's cached step list, so opening a second device on the same run costs nothing.

THE STEP

Every step row opens to the report it produced (outputMarkdown). It is fetched one step at a time, on expand: it is a whole rendered document per step, and carrying forty of them with the list would be most of a megabyte of text nobody has opened. It renders as text, never as HTML -- a step's output is not something a dashboard should let script the page it is read on.

The Exception cell now carries the platform's own output status message on hover. It is a paragraph, so it cannot be a column, and it is the thing an exception status is asking you to read.

THE SUMMARY

- Steps complete, Steps failed and Exceptions are now buttons: each selects the chip that produces its own number, opens the filter panel so the filter is visible, and clears on a second click.
- Added run groups Done and Running, counted from totalSteps against totalStepsComplete -- the run group's own declared counters, which count steps that have not produced a record yet.

THE TIME SCALE

48 hours, 72 hours, 5 days, 15 days and 60 days join 24h / 7d / 30d / 90d / all.

Also: the per-device phase prefetch is retired, because neither remaining view has a per-device phase list for it to warm.

1.0.18 -- the step STATUS column was showing the queue state, not the outcome.

A step carries three picklists that disagree on purpose: status is the outcome, queueStatus is the worker-queue state, and outputStatus is whether the output was clean. Every aggregate asked for queueStatus and aliased it "status", so a finished run whose queue rows were never reset read as IN PROGRESS at 5/5 steps, 100%. One lab box had 683 steps parked at queueStatus=Running against 1179 that had actually completed.

The outcome now wins, and the queue state is kept only as a fallback for a step that has no outcome yet. Both columns are fetched so either can answer.

Failures were undercounted for the same reason: the failure slice filtered queueStatus=Fail, which found 5 rows on a box with 16 real failures. It filters the outcome now.

Status spellings are normalized through one synonym table, because the vocabulary is not stable across boxes -- "Canceled" on one, "Cancelled" on another. An unmapped spelling used to fall through to pending, and pending reads as still-running, so a single letter could hold a finished fleet at IN PROGRESS. Anything the table does not cover now lands in its own bucket and is named on the run row as "N unknown", counted as finished rather than as progress.

1.0.17 -- the six filter axes moved behind a Filters button next to the search box.

They were the widest thing on the page: six rows of wrapping chips pushed the run list a couple of hundred pixels down the tile, and most sessions narrow once and then read the list. The panel now opens on demand, and the list starts where the filters used to sit.

The button carries the number of active selections across every axis, so a shut panel still says how many filters are narrowing the list beneath it, and Clear filters stays on screen next to it. A panel that hid an active filter would be the same unseeable state the widget already refuses to create within a single axis.

The open/shut choice rides the render snapshot, so a dashboard refresh -- which remounts the widget outright -- does not spring the panel back open.

1.0.16 -- the report is about RUN GROUPS, DEVICES, STEPS and AUTOMATION ACTIONS, not about upgrading.

Every "upgraded" reading is gone. The widget used to call a device upgraded whenever it finished the steps it was given, which is a guess about what the automation did and is wrong for any run that is not a firmware push -- a pre-check sweep, a config diff, an HA identity collection. The axes are now the ones the records actually carry, so a new action added next year is counted without the widget knowing what it means.

Filtering, rebuilt:
- The time scale sits on a row of its own, first. It is not another chip: every vocabulary below is read out of the run groups inside it, so a chip that would select nothing is never offered.
- Six filter axes, one row each, in the order an operator narrows: run group name, tag, device, automation action, step status, and step exception status. Pick one or many of each. OR within an axis, AND across them.
- Step status (did it run) and step exception status (was its output clean) are separate axes on purpose -- a step can complete and still report exceptions, and that is usually the finding the run was dispatched to make.
- A long axis collapses to a few values plus "+N more", and always draws in full while something in it is selected.

The list and the summary:
- A run group is shown when any of its steps matches everything selected.
- Each run row carries a progress bar of steps complete over total steps.
- Expanding a run lists every step in it: device, step name, automation action, status, exception status and step time. Clicking any cell filters by it. This replaces the old per-device drill-down, which cost a click and a request per device to reach steps that name their device anyway.
- The summary band recomputes from the run groups on screen, so it can never describe a wider set than the list under it.

Performance: all of the above is one additional aggregate query per load (grouped by run, device, action, status and exception) plus one per run when it is expanded. Nothing pulls step records, which is what kept a large fleet renderable in the first place.

Also fixed: the per-device step prefetch no longer runs in the Runs view, where there are no per-device rows left for it to warm.

metadata.description: Report over the ZTPf2 modules, built around the run group -- the unit an operator actually dispatches -- and pivotable onto the device. Filters, time scale and summary sit above both views and narrow one shared fact cube, so the numbers always describe the list beneath them. A run group's verdict is its own status field; steps in flight are counted from the step's own done flag. Every step expands to its rendered output report, and deep-links to its record. CSV exports for steps, devices, run groups and failures, plus a print-ready PDF.
